title:
Space engineering
Radio frequency and modulation
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Working Group)
status_notes: Rev. 2 of 4 October 2011 ('Second issue revision 2'), following ECSS-E-50-05A (14 November 2007), ECSS-E-50-05B (never issued), ECSS-E-ST-50-05C (31 July 2008) and ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Rev. 1 (6 March 2009); the Rev. 2 changes are marked with revision tracking (change log, p. 3). The document does not state that it is superseded, and no later issue is in the library.

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Frequency allocations to the Space Operation, Space Research and Earth Exploration-Satellite services
Specific conditions for the use of certain frequency bands
Turnaround frequency ratio for coherent transponders
Spacecraft-Earth station interface control document - DRD (normative)

key_points.text: Rev. 2 removes filtered-OQPSK from the 8 400 MHz - 8 450 MHz band and aligns Annex D.2.2 and the bibliography with CCSDS 401.0-B-20 (April 2009) instead of 401.0-B-17.

Scope: radio communication techniques for spacecraft-Earth station links in both directions and for tracking; applicable to spacecraft supported by Earth stations (not by data relay satellites) in the Space Operation, Space Research and Earth Exploration-Satellite services, the latter including Meteorological Satellite.
Category A: altitude less than 2 × 10^6 km; category B and 'deep space': 2 × 10^6 km or more [ITU/RR/1.177].

Primary allocations include 2 025–2 110 MHz (SR, SO, EES, Earth-space), 2 200–2 290 MHz (SR, SO, EES, space-Earth), 7 145–7 190 MHz and 8 400–8 450 MHz (deep space), 8 025–8 400 MHz (EES space-Earth) and 31 800–32 300 / 34 200–34 700 MHz (deep space).

Coherent turnaround ratios (fup/fdown) include 221/240 for S-band up/S-band down and 749/880 for X-band up/X-band down; band pairs should come from Table 5-1, otherwise Table 5-2 shall be used. The ratios derive from CCSDS 401.0-B-20.

Telecommand PCM symbol rates are 4 000/2^n sps (n = 0..9, NRZ-L or NRZ-M on a subcarrier) or 4 000 × 2^n sps (n = 1..6, SP-L); NRZ-M is not used for category B, and 4 ksps only with the 16 kHz subcarrier.
SP-L shall only be used for direct modulation of the RF carrier (no subcarrier), and NRZ waveforms only on a subcarrier; SP-L is also known as bi-phase or Manchester encoding.
Telecommand subcarriers are 8 or 16 kHz sine waves; above 4 ksps telecommand symbols are SP-L encoded directly on the carrier.
For NRZ telemetry above 60 ksps no subcarrier is used: SP-L direct modulation up to 1 Msps at S and X band, or suppressed-carrier modulation per clause 6.2.

Data transition density shall be at least 125 (category A) or 275 (category B) per 1 000 consecutive symbols, with runs of ones or zeros limited to 64 symbols; otherwise the ECSS-E-ST-50-01 clause 9 pseudo-randomizer shall be used.

Peak modulation index limits: telecommand NRZ 0,2-1,4 rad, telecommand SP-L 0,2-1,0 rad, telemetry sine subcarrier max 1,5 rad, ranging Earth-space 0,1-1,4 rad, ranging space-Earth 0,01-0,7 rad; combined Earth-space index should not exceed 1,75 rad.
Residual carrier power shall exceed -15 dBc (space-Earth) and -10 dBc (Earth-space).
Suppressed-carrier modulation shall be used for telemetry above 1 Msps; above 2 Msps (bands below 8 500 MHz) or 20 Msps (31,8-32,3 GHz) only TCM 8PSK, filtered OQPSK or GMSK shall be used.
If the ground network can resolve phase ambiguity from the sync marker, no differential encoding is used for BPSK/QPSK/OQPSK/UQPSK; otherwise differential encoding shall be performed.

Uplink acquisition at 2 025-2 110 MHz (category A): unmodulated carrier swept with a symmetrical triangular waveform; recommended max sweep rate 32 kHz/s, max discontinuity 10 Hz, max sweep range ±150 kHz for a 2BL = 800 Hz transponder PLL; transponder lock reported in telemetry (CLCW).

The spacecraft-Earth station ICD is drafted in Phase B and follows the normative DRD of Annex A (stations, equipment configuration, performances, applicable TT&C standards and waivers, link parameter choices, TT&C operational modes).
Annex D: unlike CCSDS 401 (2.2.3), only NRZ-L is recommended for category B telecommand; filtered OQPSK is restricted to specific filters, and SRRC-4D 8PSK TCM only to 2,0 and 2,5 b/s/Hz.
ITU Radio Regulations cannot be tailored; tailoring should be supported by the frequency coordinator.

notes: Slug 'rev24october2011' means 'Rev. 2, 4 October 2011'. The extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in document IDs; many Greek letters and symbols (degrees, alpha, less-or-equal) are dropped from the text, e.g. '±5 of that of a perfect PSK signal' (p. 42) and the GMSK/TCM equations in clause 9 (p. 64) and Annex C (p. 74) are garbled. Footnote 16 still cites 'ECSS-E-50-02A' for ranging (p. 45), and the bibliography lists the companion standards ECSS-E-ST-50-02 and -50-04 undated; the bibliography footnote notes that SFCG/HB is in fact a normative publication (p. 80). Annex C reproduces a table numbered 'Table 1' inside Figure C-1 (p. 76). Companions in the library: ECSS-E-ST-50-02C (ecss-e-st-50-02c31july2008), ECSS-E-ST-50-01C (ecss-e-st-50-01c31july2008), ECSS-E-ST-50-04C (ecss-e-st-50-04c31july2008), ECSS-E-HB-50A (ecss-e-hb-50a-15november2008). CCSDS 401.0-B is in the library at a later issue (ccsds-401-0-401x0b32), not at the -20 issue cited here. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 81 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 80.
